capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction and use the standard geometric characterizations.

- For the open immersion \(f:X\to Y\), the restriction of \(f\) identifies every open \(U\subseteq X\) with the open \(f(U)\subseteq Y\), which is precisely `Scheme.Hom.opensFunctor f U`. The corresponding restricted schemes are isomorphic, so one is affine exactly when the other is affine.

- For the second statement, use the finite-fiber criterion: a morphism locally of finite type is locally quasi-finite exactly when every topological fiber is discrete. The displayed preimage of \(\{x\}\), with its subtype topology, is exactly the underlying topological space of the scheme-theoretic fiber over \(x\). Locally on affine charts, this fiber is the spectrum of a finitely generated algebra over the residue field \(\kappa(x)\). Such a spectrum is discrete exactly when it is zero-dimensional; finite generation then makes it Artinian, hence finite, yielding quasi-finiteness. Conversely, a locally quasi-finite morphism has discrete fibers.

The locally-of-finite-type assumption is essential in the converse: it supplies quasi-compactness/finiteness of the discrete fibers and allows the standard quasi-finiteness criterion to apply.
